listing_view.reasoning: Subscription stood only at ~0.99 times as of mid-morning on day one [figures: subscription_history], meaning the book was barely covered with three days left, which is tepid for an issue priced at 0.403 of its stated peer-average P/E. A barely-covered book on day one in a price band of Rs 258-272 suggests no strong demand mood; the issue may limp to full subscription via QIB/HNI late bids, but there is no evidence of enthusiasm here.

longterm_view.reasoning: Free cash flow was negative in two of the last three years and the latest-year operating cash flow of Rs 97.85 million was swamped by Rs 698.82 million of capex, so the business consumes cash even when profitable [figures: free_cash_flow, operating_cash_flow]. The claimed Rs 3,200 million fresh issue (which I cannot fully verify from the flattened table) therefore looks like the real financing story. Sticky customers (nine-year average tenure [business, page 219]) and integration [business, page 221] are positives, but a 51.6x P/E is not priced for a cash-hungry manufacturer unless growth and margins both hold.

governance.reasoning: No criminal proceedings against promoters and no SEBI disciplinary actions are asserted [litigation, page 408; litigation, page 409], and margin money pledged against borrowings is modest at Rs 73-77 million [promoters, page 332]. However, related-party transactions exist and are only cross-referenced, not disclosed in the extracts given [promoters, page 289; related_party, page 406], so I cannot verify the claim of no promoter conflict [promoters, page 287].

key_risks.why_it_matters: Two of three years were free-cash-flow negative and cumulative capex far exceeds operating cash generation, so equity holders fund the growth engine and dilution/debt recurs.

key_risks.risk: Value anchor is an unverifiable benchmark P/E of 128
key_risks.why_it_matters: The document makes the issue look cheap at 0.403 of a 128x peer average, but zero peer rows could be parsed and verified, so the discount may be an artefact of a poorly chosen peer set rather than genuine cheapness.
At ~0.99x subscription by late morning of day one, the offer depends on late institutional money; failed or marginal subscription would signal pricing power lies with buyers, not the seller.
Related-party dealings are acknowledged but only by cross-reference, and I could not read their scale from the material supplied, a standard place value leaks in Indian mid-caps.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: I cannot verify it. The document quotes an industry average P/E of 128.11 and my extraction confirmed zero peer rows, so I do not know who the peers are or whether 128x reflects inflated peers. A 128x peer average for cable manufacturers is itself an extraordinary number that smells of an expensive peer set or a skewed average; the 51.6x asking multiple only looks cheap against that possibly-inflated benchmark, not in any absolute sense. Treat the 'discount' as unproven.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A verified peer table showing the 128x average is genuinely representative (which would reframe 51.6x as cheap), and either a strong final-day QIB subscription or a clean debt/ROE read from the balance sheet chapter would move the listing and long-term scores respectively.
